```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
```

## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
summary(cars)
```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.

First I must load the datasets into my R markdwon file 
``` {r}
rep_2018 <- read_csv("00_rep_candidates_2018.csv")
rep_2022 <- read_csv("00_rep_candidates_2022.csv")
dem_2018 <- read_csv("00_dem_candidates_2018.csv")
dem_2022 <- read_csv("00_dem_candidates_2022.csv")

```
Next it's time to start cleaning names 
```{r}
rep_2018 <- rep_2018 %>%
  janitor::clean_names()

rep_2022 <- rep_2022 %>%
  janitor::clean_names()

dem_2018 <- dem_2018 %>%
  janitor::clean_names()

dem_2022 <- dem_2022 %>%
  janitor::clean_names()


# --- make primary_percent columns consistent ---

rep_2018 <- rep_2018 %>%
  mutate(primary_percent = as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.]", "", primary_percent)))

rep_2022 <- rep_2022 %>%
  mutate(primary_percent = as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.]", "", primary_percent)))

dem_2018 <- dem_2018 %>%
  mutate(primary_percent = as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.]", "", primary_percent)))

dem_2022 <- dem_2022 %>%
  mutate(primary_percent = as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.]", "", primary_percent)))




# combine and tag each dataset with party + year
candidates <- bind_rows(
  rep_2018 %>% mutate(party = "Republican", year = 2018),
  rep_2022 %>% mutate(party = "Republican", year = 2022),
  dem_2018 %>% mutate(party = "Democrat",  year = 2018),
  dem_2022 %>% mutate(party = "Democrat",  year = 2022)
)

# quick check
glimpse(candidates)
table(candidates$party)
```
Now to drop columns


```{r}
rep_2018 <- rep_2018 %>%
  janitor::remove_empty(c("rows", "cols")) %>%
  drop_na(candidate, state)

rep_2022 <- rep_2022 %>%
  janitor::remove_empty(c("rows", "cols")) %>%
  drop_na(candidate, state)

dem_2018 <- dem_2018 %>%
  janitor::remove_empty(c("rows", "cols")) %>%
  drop_na(candidate, state)

dem_2022 <- dem_2022 %>%
  janitor::remove_empty(c("rows", "cols")) %>%
  drop_na(candidate, state)




# Add year + combine all datasets
candidates <- bind_rows(
  dem_2018 %>% mutate(party = "Democrat", year = 2018),
  dem_2022 %>% mutate(party = "Democrat", year = 2022),
  rep_2018 %>% mutate(party = "Republican", year = 2018),
  rep_2022 %>% mutate(party = "Republican", year = 2022)
)

# Compute average primary percentage by year
avg_primary_by_year <- candidates %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarize(
    avg_primary = mean(primary_percent, na.rm = TRUE),
    count = n()
  )

# Visualize the libe plot
ggplot(avg_primary_by_year, aes(x = factor(year), y = avg_primary, group = 1)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", size = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "darkblue") +
  labs(
    title = "Average Primary Vote Percentage by Year",
    x = "Election Year",
    y = "Average Primary %"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
Next check the amount of rows/columns and make sure everything looks good

```{r check-clean}
glimpse(rep_2018)
glimpse(rep_2022)
glimpse(dem_2018)
glimpse(dem_2022)
names(rep_2018)
```


```{r}
# --- Load libraries ---
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)

# --- Read in all candidate files ---

# --- Combine them into one dataset ---
candidates <- bind_rows(dem_2018, rep_2018, dem_2022, rep_2022)

# --- Optional: print summary ---
glimpse(candidates)


# Example for Democrats 2022
ggplot(dem_2022, aes(x = primary_percent)) +
  geom_histogram(
    bins = 30,
    fill = "#2E86AB",
    color = "white"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Primary Vote Percentages (Democrats 2022)",
    x = "Primary Percent",
    y = "Number of Candidates"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


```



``` {r}

# columns we actually need for the primary metrics
common_vars <- c("candidate", "state", "primary_outcome", "incumbent")

all_cands <- bind_rows(
  rep_2018 %>%
    dplyr::select(all_of(common_vars)) %>%
    mutate(party = "Republican", year = 2018),

  rep_2022 %>%
    dplyr::select(all_of(common_vars)) %>%
    mutate(party = "Republican", year = 2022),

  dem_2018 %>%
    dplyr::select(all_of(common_vars)) %>%
    mutate(party = "Democrat", year = 2018),

  dem_2022 %>%
    dplyr::select(all_of(common_vars)) %>%
    mutate(party = "Democrat", year = 2022)
)

# quick check
dplyr::glimpse(all_cands)
```
